column2: Marriage of Betty Brett and Will Hamlin
The faculty announces the admission to the Senior Division of Mary Brett, Nell Goldsmith, Bill McLaughlin, and Ruth Miller
Eric Bentley leaves for Nashville to teach history and English literature at the Fisk University summer session
Josef Albers leaves for Groton (Lowthorpe School); back at Lake Eden on July 16 to direct the Summer Art Institute
Mrs. Bertha Ostrow, Carol's mother, and her young son Jarold arrive from Cincinnati
Work between quarters: South Lodge wing, central attic of South Lodge (six beds), Studies Building corridors paneled in chestnut, floors sanded
Rudolph Freund (Charlottesville) arrives for two weeks
Private Ralph Tyler arrives for twenty-four hours
The upper floor of the South Lodge wing is finished: a living room, three bedrooms, and a bathroom handed over to the kitchen staff
The Board of Fellows announces the appointment of Alfred Kazin as visiting lecturer in English and American literature for the fall quarter 1944-45
Cynthia Carr arrives from Gulfport for a four-day furlough
Sergeant Jack Swackhamer arrives from Camp Carson for a five-day furlough
Ruth Brancher (Office of War Information) arrives for a week to study the college for an article for overseas
Roland Johnson, a friend of the Henry Leonards, visiting
Weekend visitors: Kedric Lynch, Herbert Oppenheimer, Jimmie Stranch
Maja Bentley leaves for a week at Fisk University, where Eric Bentley is teaching
Josef Albers returns to Lake Eden to direct the Summer Art Institute
Clark Foreman, on leave from the college, is appointed to the CIO Political Action Committee by Sidney Hillman
Mr. Baskett, librarian of the University of Georgia, visiting early in the week
Corporal Dan Heffrey arrives for six days with his uncle and aunt, the Nikolai Graudans
Ruth O'Neill comes back to resume her studies after a year away
Yella Pessl plays a Haydn concerto with orchestra at the Piedmont Festival
Sergeant Albert Haig, from the Lake Lure rest center, spends the weekend with the Henry Leonards
Emil Holzhauer and Miss Blackburn (Wesleyan College, Macon) invited to dinner
Arrival of Mrs. Kenneth Robinson (Denver)
Photographs by Joseph Breitenbach displayed on the dining hall panels
Maja Bentley and Jane Stone go to New York to take their graduation orals before Jacques Barzun and Lionel Trilling
Herbert A. Miller leaves for Temple University (Philadelphia) to teach general sociology and world minorities for six weeks
Joseph Breitenbach goes back to his New York studio

Recital of compositions by Ursula Lewis, a Music Institute student (including two songs premiered in New York in the spring); then Jeannette Siegel plays the slow movement of her unfinished piano sonata
Maude Dabbs, a former student, comes from Mayesville (South Carolina) for two days
Gisela Kronenberg arrives from Chicago for ten days at Lake Eden
Panel “Learning and Intuition in Music Education,” second in the series, led by Ernest Bacon (Converse College)
Former students visiting: John Campbell, Gisela Kronenberg, Otis Levy, Judy Mandelbaum, A. Nimmanahaeminda; and Alvin Lustig, who is preparing a quarterly magazine of the visual arts
The student crews, helped by six men from the 134th Field Artillery, bring in 85 tons of silage
Haymaking: 21 acres of soybeans to harvest, with the soldiers of the 134th Field Artillery

Work program: last loads of silage on Monday, silage cutter returned to the orphanage, which Max Penley helps for three days; cabbages sold in Asheville, wood sawed, hog fattening pen; tennis court fence removed (Ken Kurtz); insulation of the Alberses' attic; partition knocked down at Black Dwarf; help from seven soldiers of the 134th Field Artillery
Anni Albers leaves by train for New York; back October 3
Ted Dreier leaves on a business trip for the college: Chapel Hill, Washington, New York; back early the following week
Fred Cohen and Elsa Kahl leave by train for New York
Alfred Kazin, the new visiting lecturer in English and American literature, arrives at Lake Eden
Heinrich and Johanna Jalowetz leave by bus for a short vacation at the Foremans' summer house in Highlands
Mimi French and Liese Kulka leave by train
William Morse Cole arrives for his eleventh annual audit of the college's accounts
George and Mrs. Zabriskie leave Durham for Lake Eden
Erwin Straus, on a sabbatical leave granted by the Board of Fellows, leaves for Baltimore: Fellow in Psychiatry at Johns Hopkins
Fritz and Maria Hansgirg due to leave Oakland (California)
Lieutenant William C. Berry expected for two days at Lake Eden
Anni Albers returns to Lake Eden
Max Paul (New York) arrives to begin his studies at the college
Sam Brown arrives in Black Mountain (his operation is postponed)
Mr. and Mrs. Theodore Rondthaler (Clemmons), guests of the college, expected Friday or Saturday
Miss Eunice Miller, Herbert Miller's sister, expected
Jane Slater returns from Ogden (Utah) after a four-week vacation, to prepare for her graduation
Ted Dreier leaves with Bobbie for a week's vacation in Florida; back the following Saturday
Visitors of the week: Clare Leighton (engraver, Duke University) with Mrs. Kennedy, Bill Berry (for the weekend), Eunice Miller, Leo Shames, Emily Harrison (Sarasota Outdoor School), Elvira Cabell
Dick Forberg goes back to Chicago after ten days at Lake Eden
Robert Wunsch leaves for Greensboro to represent the college at the 24th annual meeting of the North Carolina College Conference; back Friday morning
Robert Wunsch returns to Lake Eden

An “opera” staged: Mozart's Don Giovanni on Fritz Hansgirg's records, with small cardboard sets by Anni Albers and Bill Reed that follow the action; Heinrich Jalowetz introduces the work before the overture
Ted and Bobbie Dreier return to Lake Eden
After the opera, Jagna Braunthal, Chuck Forberg, Molly Gregory, Ati Gropius, and Anna Schauffler hike up to the pasture; back Sunday morning
Janet Heling sings, accompanied by Henrietta Barth, at the Mountain View Church service (a prelude by Pachulski to her own words)
Fire at the college dump shortly before lunch, quickly brought under control
Ted and Bobbie Dreier return after ten days at Coronado Beach (Florida)

New organization of the Work Program: one volunteer crew for each type of work, each with its coordinator (Janie Stone kitchen, Egbert Swackhamer hauling, Ann MacKinnon housekeeping, Chuck Forberg furnaces…)

Visitors of the week: Roger Milian (weaver), the Rondthalers (weekend), Dr. Elise Teller (Highland Hospital) and Miss Parks (Pack Memorial Library), invited to dinner on Saturday and to the concert, Miss Sarah Loftin
Trudi Straus, Gretel Lowinsky, and Anna Schauffler serenade the Fritz Hansgirgs (a Beethoven trio) on their first evening in their new house
The concert intermission is extended by half an hour to listen to Roosevelt's campaign speech in Boston
Visitors of the week: Privates Peter Cornell and Russel Casey (Camp Croft) and Corporal Marshal Gorham (Greenville)
Election day: the college's voters go down to Black Mountain to vote
Several students and faculty members stay up late to hear the election returns
Mrs. Elizabeth Boyden leaves for Washington for treatment by an eye doctor
Death of Frances Goldman
Open house at the Fritz Hansgirgs' in the Stone Cottage
Ralph B. Bridgman, president of Hampton Institute, expected to talk about his plan for a summer institute at Hampton
Mr. and Mrs. Raymond Trayer expected for a week
Betty Kelley's eukinetics class (Monday and Thursday evenings until the end of the quarter)
Ted Dreier leaves for New York and New England on a business trip for the college
Contemporary Problems course: Rabbi Robert P. Jacobs (Asheville) on the approach of Jewish organizations

Herbert Miller and four students (Henrietta Barth, Jagna Braunthal, Janet Rees, Eleanor Smith) represent the college at the “Design for Living Today” conference in Greensboro; back on Sunday in Miller's car
First snow and sleet of the season
Contemporary Problems course: Father Michael Carey (Swannanoa) on the Catholic approach
“Christmas came by mail”: Nell Goldsmith plays Santa Claus and hands out packages of cigarettes sent to the alumni
Work on the dances and songs begins in the rehearsals of the children's play
Economies: the Work Program takes over the cleaning of the Studies Building, the offices, and the library, in place of the paid staff
Father Michael Carey, the Swannanoa parish priest, visits the campus
Alfred Kazin leaves for Washington to prepare his papers for England, where in January he will study the education of soldiers for the Office of War Information
Birth of Anthony Walcott, son of Duncan and Barbara Dwight
Contemporary Problems course: the Reverend Grady Hardin (Black Mountain) on the Protestant approach
The delegates to the Greensboro “Design for Living Today” conference finish their report
The cast of the children's play gives a fifteen-minute broadcast; recording rebroadcast on Friday, December 1
Curtiss Cowan paints the flats for the play on the dining hall porch
Rebroadcast of the recording of the children's play program
Last changes to the costumes and sets of the children's play, between dinner and midnight
Ted Dreier comes back by train after a two-week business trip to New York and New England
William Morse Cole: talk on “Corporations” (third lecture on economics)
Sunday, December 10 is a class day: Friday's classes in the morning, Thursday's in the afternoon
Expected candidates: Dr. Maurice Gramer (English), David H. Corkran (history), James B. Hill (business management, Bob Orr's position)
The truck takes the luggage to the express office and the bus station in Black Mountain
